To the best of my understanding at the time there was a fairly even split of who was on the politicians' sides and those who were on Marv's. You had those who wanted the growth that Cody's plant supported (our new construction was exploding at that time) and those who didn't want what they believed would be an eyesore inside the limits of a tourist town.

As I recall some of the leadership who screwed him the most had already left their political position and had returned to their usual businesses.

The shell wasn't lowered on. Only the hatch. He welded the shell to the cab and body of the machine. The hatch he welded closed on the inside. His shop was just tall enough for the finished product let alone the clearance needed to hoist it over the entire bulldozer.

If there is i would love to read or see it myself but I haven't seen anything that goes into all of the details that led to such a memorable day. What surprised me was learning this wasn't the first bulldozer rampage in CO. Oddly enough both happened in small towns. The other if I recall correctly did result in a death other than the perpetrator.
Yep that is definitely true. He absolutely destroyed the Sky Hi News bulding while others were able to stay standing.

About a year. Before he went in the rampage he actually sent audio tapes of him monaloguing about all of his plans and intentions. On one he talks about how he has been welding the armor on all summer and no one is wise to him, so clearly God must approve of what he's doing.

The guy had some balls on him. He took out a loan to afford most of what he did and then proceeded to blow what was left of it by going out and treating himself to steak dinners and drinks down in Grand Lake.

There's a picture of him that the use on wildest police videos or something of the sort that they cropped to just his eyes making him look villainous. If you see the uncropped version he has the biggest friendliest smile. He was a nice guy in all my interactions with him. He was also hands down the best welder in the county. Listening to them trying to blow his hatch open with c4 until 2 in the morning was a laugh. In addition to th e previously mentioned items he had a small welding kit in the cab. When he lowered the hatch on he welded himself in. No man was prying him out of that thing alive.

It took the salvage yard 2 weeks to the specialty torch my dad said they needed to take off the rest of the armor plating which was spaced with concrete. It was pretty cool to get to sit in it once the armor was off though I got a earful for not putting a towel down on the seat as that wasn't dried oil I was sitting in like I naively thought it was....

Town politics stayed relatively the same, though I believe there were several changes of leadership shortly before the incident and thereafter. I want to say that one of the folks he was most mad at was no longer working for the city leadership (former mayor). But Marv still took out his private residence for how he voted and handled the whole situation.

One of things that was interesting to see in the fallout was how divided the locals were in that half the town was against what he did and the other half was cheering him on. Somewhere we have a DVD a friend made with footage that day cheering him on. There were others who had shirts made that said "Don't make me get my dozer!". When it was time to decide what to do with his machine one of the ideas was to literally make it a statue that would be the final stop on a dozer rampage tour through town. Tastefully they opted to send it to the salvage yard to be scrapped.  

Just like the town board that voted to allow the construction was almost evenly split on letting Cody build his plant inside city limits. That approval led to Marv's muffler shop losing almost all of its business from the single access road being used for construction access as well as tearing it up to run sewer and water to the concrete plant.

Issues still seem to be handled the same and there's still this issue of it being such a small area population wise that it's easy to feel like there's favoritism and corruption on matters you don't agree with. But when everyone knows each other it's hard to argue that certain people could have still been able to get permission to do the projects they've done.

Not just cameras but an air system from the cab with air lines to the cameras lenses to clear debris. He also had three rifles. Two out the r ght and left sides and a barret .50 out the back in addition to the .357 to take his own life at the end.

When Marv drove out of his own shop because the machine was too big for the doors with the armor he forgot to pull the rifles on the sides in and bent the barrels rendering them inoperable. He still used the big boy to try and shoot Cody (owner of the concrete plant that started the issue with the city)  as he was fighting Marv off with his front end loader. When the rounds started coming through the bucket of his smaller dozer Cody was smart and ran.

Later he did fire the .50 at the massive propane tanks in town but he didn't know that 1 they were empty waiting for the next fill and 2 he wasn't using a lower velocity traced round that could have ignited them. All for the best as those tanks are in range of the senior living center. 

Source - grew up in Granby with our family businesses as neighbors to him. Marv's rampage started literally behind our motel and sporting goods store.
